quests.title: A Grueling Combat Simulation

dialogue.t: Failed?
I failed again...
There's definitely something wrong with your balancing. Even if you brought in those combat specialists from the Special Assignments Battalion, nobody would be able to beat it!
Then train harder and reflect on your mistakes. It's not just a shooting simulation, either. Building defensive fortifications is just as important.
But when you demonstrated it yourself, didn't a single mistake cause the whole run to fall apart?
So what? That's exactly how dangerous the Shadow Realm should be.
If it's made even a little easier, ordinary marksmen will start having illusions of competence, thinking, "Maybe I could survive in the Shadow Realm."
So if you don't train to the strictest standards, how can you hope to perform flawlessly in such a brutal environment?
Hmm, I guess you're right.
I'm gonna go figure this thing out. No way I'm getting shut out every single run.
Oof, she really got the wind knocked out of her sails...
Looks like your tabletop game really threw her for a loop.

dialogue.sit: To be fair, a difficulty spike like that can be pretty stressful.
You probably shouldn't expect such flawless execution.

dialogue.t: A game? To you, maybe. A fun little pastime, even. But for those who know what the Shadow Realm is, the very premise of the combat simulation is enough to make them uneasy.
I created it as a way to train strategic thinking through simulations.
To the adventurers, hunters, and warriors of Snezhnaya, the Shadow Realm has always been a blade hidden deep within the snowstorms, waiting to strike.
No one knows exactly what's inside. All we can do is piece together scattered scraps of information and try to imagine just how dangerous it might be.
Then we come up with hypothetical battle plans and use them to sharpen our skills. If we're ever unlucky enough to end up in that hellhole, at least we'd stand a better chance of making it out alive.
The problem is, even at my best, I can barely survive a few rounds myself — so what chance do they have...?
Whoa... This is way more serious than Paimon was expecting.
Still, {NICKNAME} has a ton of experience with this stuff. Surely one of the best in Snezhnaya, right?
...That's true... but...

dialogue.sit: If the pay is good enough...
I could give everyone a demonstration.

dialogue.t: That raises an important question: what's a fair price for an exclusive demonstration from you, {NICKNAME}?
I honestly have no idea. I'll start by paying the equivalent of three S-rank commissions out of my own savings, then use the results to persuade the Guild to fund the project.
And if that still isn't enough, I'll have to take out a loan from the Northland Bank...

dialogue.sit: You don't need to go that far.
As long as the offer comes with genuine sincerity.

dialogue.t: Exactly! If it's something that benefits everyone, we're not about to charge an arm and a leg for it...
Actually, we've never charged outrageous prices in the first place! Knowing we've helped a lot of people is reward enough for both of us.
Thank you so much!
Then I'd better rinse my eyes with ice water and brace myself for {NICKNAME}'s demonstration.
So allow me to briefly explain the rules of the simulation...

quests.description: Talalikhin, an adventurer devoted to researching dangerous phenomena, is conducting some form of simulation training near the Adventurers’ Guild Headquarters…
